chunks: With the preceding chains of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Abu Yahya, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, say:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family, ascended the pulpit, and the colour of his cheeks changed and his complexion flickered. Then he turned towards the people with his face and said: 'O assembly of Muslims, I have been sent with the Hour as close as these two' — then he put together his two index fingers. Then he said: 'O assembly of Muslims, indeed the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, and the best of speech is the Book of Allah, and the worst of matters are innovations. Be it known that every innovation is misguidance, and be it known that every misguidance leads to the Fire. O people, whoever leaves behind wealth, it is for his family and his heirs; and whoever leaves behind weaklings or poor dependents, they are my responsibility and upon me.'

key_terms.المنبر: The pulpit (minbar) from which the Prophet delivered sermons in the Mosque of Medina
key_terms.بدعة: Bid'ah — religious innovation not sanctioned by the Quran or Sunnah
key_terms.كتاب الله: The Book of Allah — a reference to the Holy Quran
key_terms.كلا أو ضياعا: Weaklings or destitute — referring to those without means or protectors

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about innovation (bid'ah) and the best guidance?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad ascended his pulpit in Medina and delivered this sermon with visible urgency — his face changing colour — to stress the closeness of the Day of Judgment. He warned the Muslim community that the best guidance is his own sunnah and the Quran, while all religious innovations (bid'ah) lead to misguidance and hellfire. He concluded by taking personal responsibility for the welfare of the vulnerable members of the community, establishing a foundational principle of Islamic social responsibility.
